uncertain.text: en la premiere ieuneſſe deſquels, le deſir de la chair bouil
uncertain.note: a small round dot sits in the space between 'ieuneſſe' and 'deſquels', at x-height rather than on the baseline and about a third the size of this fount's full stops (compare the point after 'maiſtreſſe,' below); taken as an ink speck and omitted. The word space itself is clearly present.

uncertain.text: (qui le faiſoit coucher auec elle) la cognut en fin, & rẽdit
uncertain.note: the mark over the e of 'rẽdit' is broad, flat and slightly wavy, quite unlike the short steep acute of 'irrité' on the line above; read as a tilde (rendit).

uncertain.text: ſieurs attribuẽt à Salomõ, & Achaz Rois, leſquels (ſelon
uncertain.note: same judgment for 'attribuẽt': the mark over the e is a broad flat stroke (tilde = attribuent), contrasted at 6x with the grave of 'à' immediately after it.

uncertain.text: ans eurent des enfaus {k}: car Salomon eut Roboam, & A-
uncertain.note: sic: 'enfaus'. The letter before the final s is unmistakably a u (open top, serifed at both shoulders) where the word wants n; a turned sort. Transcribed as printed. The marker after it is the italic k of this fount (looped ascender plus a z-shaped leg) and can look like a capital K at reading size.

uncertain.text: chaz eutEzechiel {l}. Mais quoy? biẽ que l'vn enfant (ſainct
uncertain.note: 'eutEzechiel' is set with no space at all — the t and the E touch — so it is transcribed closed up per §1. The marker after 'Ezechiel' is the small italic l with a looped ascender.

uncertain.text: en teſmoin, qu'il ne mẽt point) DOMINO TESTE, dit-
uncertain.note: DOMINO TESTE is set in letterspaced small capitals; closed up per §3 and recorded by spaced_caps on the block. The same for NON MENTIOR on the next line.

uncertain.text: auſsi gens de literature grãde, & recõmẽdable foy: tou-
uncertain.note: the line-end mark after 'tou' is a short thick wedge sitting lower than the thin slanted hyphen of 'dit-' two lines above; read as the word-break sign of 'tou|tesfois' and transcribed '-' per §1, but it could be read as a full stop.

uncertain.text: le cõte de leurs ans.'Tant y a, que quand biẽ cela ſeroit
uncertain.note: a raised comma-shaped sort stands between the full stop of 'ans.' and the T of 'Tant', at ascender height; transcribed as an apostrophe as printed. It makes no sense in the sentence and may be foul case.

uncertain.text: deuancier, & plus libre, que Platon, niAriſtote: à ſçauoir,
uncertain.note: 'niAriſtote' is set with the i and the A all but touching — the gap is a small fraction of the word space in 'que Platon,' on the same line — so it is transcribed closed up per §1. Also, the d of 'deuancier' at the line start is a filled ink blot; read as d from sense and from the surviving ascender.

the final a is heavily inked and carries a short slanted stroke above it that could be read as a tilde ('lã'); 'Gloſe en la ſomme' is the sense, so it is read as a plain a with a stray mark. The line does end there — there is clear white space to its right.
the mark between 'xx' and 'q.' is set high and looks like a short dash rather than a point; read as the full stop the citation form requires (xx. q. i.).
a small dot sits between 'ſon' and 'diction'; much smaller than the note's commas and full stops, so taken as a speck. The word ends in a full n (the next line begins 'naire'), not a tilde.

the note's key letter is an italic k — a looped ascender plus a z-shaped leg — which at reading size looks like the two letters 'lz'. Read as key k, matching the {k} marker in the body. The first letter of 'Io.' is drawn with the same loop as the italic l, so the line could be read 'lo. And.'; 'Io. And. & Panor.' (Ioannes Andreae and Panormitanus) is the sense.
a small raised tick is printed between 'Panor.' and 'au'; transcribed as an apostrophe. It may be a broken sort or an offset mark.

the middle of the first word shows two strokes carrying what look like one or two dots, so it could be read 'diix.' or 'diux.'; 'dux.' (de eo qui duxit) is the reading taken. The ſ of 'cõſ.' is a long s.

the last letter has a closed bowl and reads as e, giving 'eſcriuane'; the sense wants 'eſcriuant' (S. Hierome eſcriuant ad Vitalem), so this may be a misprint or an inked-in italic t. Transcribed as read.
the mark after the swash italic D has a tail below the baseline and is read as a comma, unlike the plain round point after 'ea.' beside it; it could be a full stop.

this foot word has no key letter of its own: it is the tail of margin note q, whose last margin line is '& au vi. des' (Platon … au vi. des loix). Recorded with key null and beside_line rather than a second entry keyed q, which would duplicate the margin note's key.
the gathering mark is printed 'A ij.' with a full stop after the j; kept as printed (p001 carries a bare 'A').

the margin is badly crowded on this page and every note after g starts well below its marker — h beside body line 9 (marker on line 6), l beside line 21 (marker on line 11), p beside line 36 (marker on line 24) — until note r is driven off the margin into the foot block. beside_line values were fixed by measuring the row positions of both columns (body pitch 45.2 px, margin pitch 36.5 px in pages/read/p003.jpg) and checked against the page image; the placements for m (line 25) and q (line 38) fall close to midway between two body lines.
